name: Königrufen Tarock
description: KÃ¶nigrufen (German: 'Calling the King') is a four-player trick-taking card game of the tarot family, played in Austria and South Tyrol. It is the most popular tarot variant in Austria and, by 2015, had become 'the favourite card game of Austrians'. The game uses a 54-card tarock pack and features a unique bidding system where players can call a king to choose a partner, along with numerous contracts and bonuses.

history.origins: KÃ¶nigrufen developed in the 18th century from earlier tarot games, incorporating the bidding principle from Spanish L'Hombre and the 'calling a king' partner selection from Quadrille. The 78-card pack was stripped to 54 cards for easier handling.
timeline: 1440s: Original tarot games emerge in Northern Italy
1730-1830: Tarock played across Europe with 78 cards
Mid-1700s: German-speaking reforms add bidding and partner calling
2015: Described as 'the favourite card game of Austrians'
history.cultural: Stronghold is Upper Austria, which hosts the Austrian Final. The game is deeply embedded in Austrian cafe culture and is considered a game requiring intelligence and tactical skill. UNESCO recognizes it as part of Austria's intangible cultural heritage.
history.evolution: The game evolved from simple tarot to a complex bidding game with numerous contracts. The bird bonuses (Trull I, Uhu, Kakadu, Marabu) were added over time, creating additional strategic layers. Regional variations developed across Austria.

setup.players: Four active players (five can participate with dealer sitting out). Partners determined by calling a King or playing solo.
setup.deck: 54-card Austrian Tarock pack: 22 trumps (Tarocks) numbered I-XXI plus SkÃ¼s, and 8 cards each in Clubs, Spades, Hearts, Diamonds.
setup.dealing: Dealer shuffles, player to left cuts. Deal in packets of 6 cards: one to each player, one to talon (middle), repeat. Each player receives 12 cards, talon has 6. Play is anticlockwise.

rules.objective: In positive contracts, declarer's side wins by taking at least 36 of 70 card points. Various contracts have different objectives (avoid tricks, win exact number of tricks, etc.).
rules.gameplay: Point-trick game with bidding. Players bid contracts; highest bidder becomes declarer. In many contracts declarer calls a king to choose a secret partner. Declarer may exchange cards with the six-card talon. After announcements (bonuses, kontras), forehand leads to the first trick. Players must follow suit if possible, otherwise must play a trump. In positive contracts declarer's side needs at least 36 of 70 card points to win; negative contracts have different objectives (e.g. lose every trick in Bettel).
keyRules: Follow suit if possible; if not, must play a trump. In positive contracts declarer's side wins with 36+ of 70 points. Talon: 6 cards; declarer may take 3 and discard 3 in Rufer-type contracts. Call a king to choose partner (holder is secret). Trull cards: Sküs, XXI (Mond), I (lowest trump) worth 5 points each. Play is anticlockwise; forehand leads first in positive contracts.

strategy.basic: In positive contracts, aim for 36+ points. Protect high-value cards (kings, honours). Remember the SkÃ¼s, XXI, and I are each worth 5 points plus their trick value.
strategy.intermediate: Talon selection is crucial. Look for packets containing kings or high trumps. When calling a king, call one you don't have - if it appears in talon, you play alone (often disadvantageous).
strategy.advanced: Bird Strategy: Announcing Pagat Ultimo, Uhu, Kakadu, or Marabu doubles their value but commits you to a specific play. Only announce if you have strong position. In negative contracts (Bettel, Piccolo), card play becomes inverted - you're trying to lose tricks, which requires understanding opponents' hands.
tips: The Mond (XXI) is vulnerable - if you hold it, be aware an opponent may try to capture it with SkÃ¼s.
In Rufer, your partner is unknown until the called king appears - play accordingly.
Valat (winning all tricks) is rare but lucrative - consider going for it with very strong hands.
Card counting is essential - track which trumps have been played.

scoring.description: Card points determine if contract is made. Game points and bonuses determine payments.
scoring.winCondition: In positive contracts declarer's side wins by taking at least 36 of 70 card points. In negative contracts (e.g. Bettel, Piccolo) objective is to lose every trick or win exactly one or two tricks. Game points and bonuses determine payments.
